To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

neurons in the anterior frontal cortex encode many of the variables required for calculating the value of choice outcomes, including probability, cost, reward and the work performed to earn the reward, and that many frontal neurons encode the value of choice outcome across multiple variables.
neurons in the ACC and OFC encode the value of different decision variables across multiple choice alternatives and that these neurons also encode the experienced outcome of the chosen alternative.
“Neurons in the anterior cignulate cortex, but not the orbitofrontal or prefrontal cortex, encode the value of choices across multiple decision variables during both choice and evaluation phases.”
In summary, our research is concerned with
how the brain evaluates choices and how this process may be disrupted in patients with frontal lobe damage.
the mechanisms that underlie decision-making, and how these mechanisms may be impaired in conditions such as schizophrenia.
the neural basis of decision‐making and the role of frontal cortical regions in encoding the value and outcome of choices.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the frontal cortex, especially ACC, encodes many variables that contribute value to the decision, and that this is a key component of its role in decision-making.
the OFC and ACC encode the value of outcomes, and that the LPFC encodes the value of the decision variables.

the OFC and ACC encode the value of outcomes by integrating multiple decision variables, and the LPFC may encode the value of these outcomes by integrating multiple representations of the value of the outcome.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the frontal cortex encodes many of the parameters necessary to evaluate the outcome of a choice, and that the ACC is particularly well suited for this function.
frontal neurons encode multiple decision parameters that enable the calculation of outcome value.
the frontal cortex is a critical brain region for the valuation of choice outcomes.
The main takeaway from our work is that
neurons in ACC, OFC and LPF encode many variables that can contribute to the valuation process, and these neurons are active both during the choice and the outcome phase of a decision‐making task.

frontal neurons encode many different variables that contribute to decision making and that these neurons often encode the value of these different choice variables across multiple decision variables (e.g., cost, benefit, probability of success, etc.) in both the choice and evaluation of choice phases of the task.

neurons in multiple regions in the frontal cortex, but particularly ACC, encode the value of outcomes, not just when making a choice, but also after the choice has been made and the outcome has been received.
